introduction: This foundational level introduces the two most transformative pedagogical shifts in 21st-century ICT education. It defines Blended Learning, explicitly details how a Flipped Classroom reverses traditional teaching, and maps these concepts to the changing role of the teacher.

core_concepts.title: What is Blended Learning?
core_concepts.description:
Blended Learning (also known as Hybrid Learning) is a formal education program that combines traditional face-to-face (brick-and-mortar) classroom methods with online digital learning activities. 
- Key Rule: It is NOT just giving students iPads in class. The student must have some control over the **time, place, path, or pace** of their learning through the digital medium.

core_concepts.title: The Flipped Classroom (A Model of Blended Learning)
core_concepts.description:
A Flipped Classroom literally 'flips' or reverses the traditional learning environment.
- Traditional Classroom: The teacher gives the lecture/teaches the concept in the classroom. The student goes home and does the 'homework' (problem-solving) alone.
- Flipped Classroom: The student receives the lecture at HOME (usually via a pre-recorded video or digital text). The student then comes to the CLASSROOM to do the 'homework' (problem-solving, projects, debates) alongside the teacher and peers.

core_concepts.title: The Pedagogical Shift in the Teacher's Role
core_concepts.description:
In a flipped/blended environment, the teacher's role completely shifts:
- From: 'Sage on the Stage' (Authoritarian knowledge transmitter delivering a 40-minute lecture).
- To: 'Guide on the Side' (Facilitator who circulates the room, helps students unstuck from complex problems, and guides collaborative group work).

core_concepts.title: Synchronous vs. Asynchronous Learning
core_concepts.description:
Essential terminology for ICT exams:
1. Synchronous Learning: Real-time learning where the teacher and students are present at the same time (e.g., Live Zoom classes, traditional physical classrooms, live webinars).
2. Asynchronous Learning: Learning that does not occur in the same place or at the same time. The student learns at their own pace (e.g., watching a pre-recorded SWAYAM video, reading an email, posting on a discussion board at midnight).

important_entities.name: Flipped Classroom = Active Learning
important_entities.key_fact: Maximizes the use of face-to-face teacher time.
important_entities.description: The greatest advantage of a Flipped Classroom is that valuable in-class time is no longer wasted on passive listening. Instead, 100% of class time is dedicated to Active Learning (Constructivism), where the teacher is physically present to correct misconceptions exactly when the student attempts to apply the knowledge.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often treat these as completely different things. **Flipped Classroom is a SUBSET of Blended Learning.** All flipped classrooms are blended learning, but not all blended learning is flipped (there are many other models of blended learning).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Homework at School, Schoolwork at Home
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To instantly identify a Flipped Classroom scenario in an exam, look for the student doing the 'listening/reading' at home and the 'doing/solving' in the classroom.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever an exam asks 'Which teaching method gives students control over the pace and time of learning while still maintaining face-to-face teacher support?', the answer is **Blended Learning**.
